sections.html: Pseudolaguvia are dwarf catfish that reach a maximum length of only 2-3 cm. Pseudolaguvia muricata becomes only 2.5-3 cm long. Origin: India.

A typical feature of the genus Pseudolaguvia is the adhesive apparatus on the belly, which looks like a broad fold. All species live in brooks or small rivers over sandy bottom. Usually the fish are found among dead plant material (detritus). In the natural habitat the water is soft and neutral.

The animals are no great swimmers, so they fit perfectly for small tanks. A tank for Pseudolaguvia should have fine sand on the bottom. Some dead leaves should also be placed in the tank. These fish are kept best at room temperature.
The catfish feed on almost any type of usual fish food – it has to fit the mouth, of course.
Pseudolaguvia are absolutely peaceful towards any tankmate, whether of their own or of different species. Plants are left unharmed.
There are rather dark colored, elongate specimens and plumper ones with a lighter coloration. In all probability this represents sexual differences.
Nothing is known so far regarding reproduction, but it is very likely that the eggs are deposited among plant material etc. and are left unguarded.

Catfishes from Asia are currently not in vogue, but many new, attractive species have been discovered recently. The first species of the genus Pseudolaguvia was discovered in 1927, but only recently was it found that the genus is species-rich. 13 of the 17 species known to date have been described from 2003 onwards.

Lexicon: Pseudolaguvia means "false Laguvia"; Laguvia is another genus of catfish. muricata means "as spiny as a shell of a Murex snail".
